recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for byte-for-byte uniform wording or reconsideration of whether each Patient Care resource needs an identifier should be handled as a new harmonization/design issue rather than as a FHIR-15780 fixup.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive STU3 Patient Care request to replace identifier definition, requirements, and comments across Patient Care resources with the global wording that treats identifier as a business identifier, not a resource logical id.
initial_application: The wording was applied in the STU3 spreadsheet era by fd64266c287a9376f6eb224be14ba8d75430a6b3 for FamilyMemberHistory, Goal, and Procedure; by 531a04bbdd2c80677236b0fb087c573811ff9fa0 for CarePlan, CareTeam, ClinicalImpression, Communication, and Flag; and by d2a0f6d8fbd7eda090adf1b40f3066fefbfeeb1f, whose subject explicitly mentions GF#15780, for AdverseEvent, AllergyIntolerance, CommunicationRequest, and Condition. Later source refactors migrated the spreadsheet wording into current StructureDefinition XML.
additional_context: FHIR-15780 is a Patient Care application of the broader GF/FHIR-15095 identifier harmonization, which is already audited on the combined branch. source/fhir.ini confirms the affected resources are active in the current build, including AdverseEvent in the active resources list; Linkage has no identifier element. Current differences such as Flag using author rather than performer and Procedure using slightly different grammar do not change the approved business-identifier meaning.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because current StructureDefinition XML for AdverseEvent, AllergyIntolerance, CarePlan, CareTeam, ClinicalImpression, Communication, CommunicationRequest, Condition, FamilyMemberHistory, Flag, Goal, and Procedure already describes identifier as a business identifier, carries the business/resource identifier comment, and states the cross-server consistency requirement.
